punchline: Start with why holds up as a communication lesson, even though the brain science Sinek hung it on doesn't.
thirty_sec: Simon Sinek argues that most companies say what they make, then how it's better, and never why they exist. Apple flips the order: a belief in challenging the status quo comes first, and the computers come last. People buy why you do it, he says, and he links that to the limbic brain. Outside critics call that brain account outdated. Still, the insight survives on marketing evidence, since belief-led brands earn loyalty while feature-led ones fight on price.
question: Is there an idea you love that you'd keep believing even if the science usually quoted to support it collapsed?
